Subject: FY27 targets & scenario playbook — exec ask + timeline

Team —

I want to kick off a compact scenario playbook for FY27 targets so we can put a clear exec ask on the Q2 board deck. The ask needs to include: top-line targets (base / conservative / upside), key levers (pricing, routing policies, Dedicated commits), and a brief contingency matrix (triggers + owners).

Goals for this thread:
- Agree on a single source-of-truth spreadsheet (I uploaded v1 below).
- Lock owners for each lever and scenario by EOD Thu so we can circulate to Finance and Sales Ops next week.
- Draft a 1-slide executive summary for QBR review by Mon 13 Apr.

I've attached FY27_Target_Scenarios_v1.xlsx — it contains a starter revenue model + sensitivity table. Please put line-item comments in the sheet; we will reconcile Friday.

Quick asks:
- Marissa: please map the sales motions and expected lift assumptions (PLG vs. enterprise).
- Aditya: compile any service-level capacity and cost assumptions for Dedicated pools.
- Laura: flag any regulatory or market risks that should change probabilities.

Thanks — I want to keep this tight and iteratively refine.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
VP, Strategy & Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FY27_Target_Scenarios_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 320KB)

Thanks Olga — I read through the workbook and added two tabs: "Motion Assumptions" and "Commit Timing". High-level notes:
- PLG uplift model assumes 12% conv to paid in base; enterprise expansion is more lumpy (we used a 30% upside for an aggressive scenario).
- I added a summary of channel-level levers (marketplace credits, sales promotions) and assigned tentative owners.

Open question for exec ask: do we call out a baseline that assumes no Dedicated reserve vs. a baseline with minimal reserved capacity? That changes cost structure materially.

I'll slot time Friday 9:30–10:30 PT to reconcile assumptions if that works for everyone.

—Marissa

Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 11:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FY27 targets & scenario playbook — exec ask + timeline

Marissa — good notes. For Dedicated capacity assumptions:
- Base: 40% of expected enterprise peak traffic on reserved pools (minimal burst).
- Conservative: 25% reserved (we shift more to hosted, higher unit cost).
- Upside: 60% reserved + negotiated GPU pricing (targeted commit).

I'll pull infra cost per token by region (US/EU) and share a short table before Friday's sync. Also tagging a risk: if we push aggressive reserved capacity without a firm pipeline commit, we expose us to utilization drag. Suggest we include a clause in the exec ask recommending staged commit (Q3 review for top-up).

Aditya
Director, Platform Economics
Redwood Inference

Olga / team —

Regulatory quick take: EU data residency will impact our conservative scenario only if we materially expand private deployments for customers. For the base and upside scenarios, flagging the following:
- Need to assume 6–8 week lead time for adding on-prem or VPC integrations at enterprise scale (this is a provisioning + security review window).
- If we push for an EU-heavy reserved capacity baseline we should separately list the incremental compliance costs (KMS, audit logging retention, legal review).

I'll add notes in the Drive and tag the items that should be in the executive appendix.

—Laura
